html:
Cusco is a city in the Andes of southern Peru, about 3,400 metres up, that was the capital of the Inca Empire. The Incas saw it as the navel of the world, where the four parts of their realm met.

It began as the seat of a small Inca kingdom, founded by tradition by Manco Cápac in the 1100s or 1200s, in a valley where the Wari had once built a provincial centre. Around 1438 the Chanka attacked it. The prince who beat them took the name Pachacuti, seized the throne and rebuilt the city in stone. He gave it its great temple of the Sun, the Coricancha, covered in gold, and the huge fortress-temple of Sacsayhuamán above it. From Cusco the Inca roads ran to every corner of the empire, and conquered rulers, such as the king of Chimor, were brought here. Royal estates such as Machu Picchu lay a few days away.

Francisco Pizarro and his men entered Cusco in 1533, after the capture of Atahualpa, and looted its gold. The Inca Manco besieged it in 1536 but could not retake it. The Spanish then made coastal Lima their capital, and built churches on Inca walls in Cusco: the convent of Santo Domingo stands on the Coricancha. The city stayed a centre of Andean life, and the rising of Túpac Amaru II in 1780 began in its region. The writer Inca Garcilaso de la Vega was born here.
sum: Cusco is a city in the Andes of southern Peru, about 3,400 metres up, that was the capital of the Inca Empire. The Incas saw it as the navel of the world, where the four parts of their realm met.
